title: Prevent local test runs from OOMing by serializing heavy Vitest suites
description:
## Problem

Running the test suites in this repo can exhaust local memory because the heaviest Vitest suites are uncapped and duplicate expensive browser/dev-server harnesses.

### Evidence
- `package.json:11-14` exposes `test:run`, `test:integration`, and `test:visual`, with `test:visual` bound directly to `vitest run --config vitest.visual.config.ts`.
- `vitest.visual.config.ts:3-9` sets only `environment`, `include`, and timeouts. It does **not** cap workers or disable file parallelism, so Vitest defaults apply.
- Local runtime on this machine reports `availableParallelism = 8`, and Vitest 1.6.x defaults to `pool=threads` and `fileParallelism=true`, so multiple visual files can execute at once.
- Every visual spec launches its own Vite dev server and its own Puppeteer browser:
  - `tests/visual/surface-smoke.test.ts:55-61`
  - `tests/visual/surface-walk-effects.test.ts:30-37`
  - `tests/visual/landing-smoke.test.ts:13-24`
  - `tests/visual/a11y-route.test.ts:8-14`
  - `tests/visual/game-flow.test.ts:9-15`
- Two of those specs also hardcode the default Vite port (`http://localhost:3000/surface/`), which means parallel runs create redundant extra dev-server processes even when only one server is actually used:
  - `tests/visual/surface-smoke.test.ts:57-59`
  - `tests/visual/surface-walk-effects.test.ts:32-34`
- The integration suite is a secondary amplifier: `vitest.integration.config.ts:7-17` also lacks worker limits while several tests allocate canvases / renderer state and iterate many frames or seeds (`tests/integration/golden-frames.test.ts:10-25`, `tests/integration/effect-interactions.test.ts:10-24`, `tests/integration/shadow-3d.test.ts:11-25`).

## Outcome

Make local test execution memory-safe on developer machines without deleting coverage.

## Proposed fix

1. **Serialize the visual suite by default**
   - Update `vitest.visual.config.ts` to disable file parallelism and explicitly cap workers at 1.
   - Prefer a process pool that avoids duplicating thread heaps for browser-heavy specs.
2. **Share the visual harness instead of re-spawning it per file**
   - Move Vite dev-server startup and Puppeteer launch into shared setup/global teardown.
   - Reuse a single server/browser per visual run when safe, instead of five independent copies.
3. **Bound integration-suite concurrency**
   - Add explicit worker limits (or targeted serial execution) for `vitest.integration.config.ts`.
   - Split the most memory-intensive cases into a dedicated config/script if needed.
4. **Make the safe path the obvious path**
   - Update package scripts/docs so the default human workflow uses the bounded configs.
   - Document when to run single-file visual tests vs the whole suite.
5. **Prove the memory regression is fixed**
   - Capture peak RSS / process counts for visual + integration runs before and after.
   - Ensure the safe defaults run successfully on a normal 8-core dev machine without OOM.

## Risks / notes

- Serializing browser tests will increase wall-clock time; if needed, CI can shard at the job level instead of local per-file parallelism.
- Reusing one browser/server requires careful cleanup between specs to avoid cross-test pollution.
design: Primary fix: cap or disable Vitest file parallelism for browser/jsdom-heavy suites. Structural follow-up: replace per-file Vite+Puppeteer startup with a shared visual harness and split any remaining memory-heavy integration cases into bounded configs. Prefer CI/job sharding over local intra-suite parallelism.
acceptance_criteria: Visual suite runs with at most one dev-server/browser harness at a time; integration suite has explicit concurrency bounds; package scripts/docs point to the safe default commands; maintainers have a verification note showing the bounded suites complete on an 8-core dev machine without OOM.
notes: Implemented bounded Vitest configs for visual/integration suites, added a shared visual globalSetup/browser harness, and documented safe local test commands in docs/testing.md. Verification: bun run test:visual -- tests/visual/a11y-route.test.ts tests/visual/surface-smoke.test.ts (pass, shared harness across 2 files); bun run test:integration -- tests/integration/hc-boot.test.ts (pass); bun run test:integration -- tests/integration/effect-interactions.test.ts tests/integration/golden-frames.test.ts showed effect-interactions passing and golden-frames failing due existing baseline hash drift, not harness/concurrency startup.

title: Reinstate theos.sh title as diegetic world object
description:
After the effects-over-surface epic (theos.sh-6uu), the animated theos.sh title was demoted: it now only renders during a pre-walk intro scene and dissolves on first input. The title is no longer a first-class persistent object.

Reinstate the title as a diegetic element in the walk world — still interactive with the pipeline, but embedded in the scene geometry rather than bolted onto a pre-walk overlay.

Candidates to evaluate:
- Floating glyph text in the middle of the torus ring (visible from the walkable surface)
- Distant sky/horizon inscription (billboard-aligned or projected onto the celestial sphere)
- Inscribed on terrain (height-map carved letters the player can walk past)
- Orbiting object above the manifold

Requirements:
- Title participates in the raycast pipeline (terrain/artifact hit path or a new HitKind)
- Title character cells route through CellState like other content, so effects (jitter, saturation-field, background-wave) still apply
- Reveal animation preserved or adapted — should not be a static print
- Works across seeds; color scheme still derived from seed
- Survives Applicator pipeline rebuilds (no title-only scene state machine)

Blocks legacy-removal (theos.sh-8vs) parity if the title's absence from the walking scene is considered a regression.
design:
Simplest path: new Artifact subtype 'title' placed at fixed (u,v) near spawn with a large offset so it floats above the torus hole. intersectNearestArtifact already handles sphere-shaped artifact intersection — extend with a glyph-grid artifact that emits character cells via a specialized shader.

Alternative: dedicated TitleObject in the scene graph with its own hitKind='title', rendered by a new march path that projects the 'theos.sh' string onto a billboard quad facing the player. Cells with hitKind='title' route to a new base contributor (parallel to surface-cells) that sets layer='face' with accent HSV.

Either way, register the title contributor in WALK_SCENE_EFFECTS so it lives inside the walk scene permanently — no scene state machine coupling.
acceptance_criteria:
- Title visible somewhere in walkable scene across at least 3 distinct seeds
- Title glyph cells flow through Applicator pipeline (test: saturation-field affects title saturation)
- No regression in surface-smoke / surface-walk-effects visual tests (update pinned hashes if intentional)
- Title survives player walking away and returning (not a one-shot)
close_reason: Title reinstated as spherical billboard at torus center; participates in raycast with new 'title' HitKind; per-char time-based reveal; scene state machine removed; 320 tests pass

title: Title logo readability fights with surface fidelity
description:
The diegetic 'theos.sh' billboard is hard to read against the
high-fidelity walk scene — noise glyphs, terrain silhouette,
contour banding, and color scheme combine to visually camouflage
the title text on first frame.

Candidates to try:
- Temporary fidelity reduction (monochrome / muted contrast) while
  title is prominent, fade back as dissolve progresses.
- Stronger shadow-halo contrast or a local desaturation disk
  around title.center.
- Larger billboard / higher density threshold so glyphs stay solid.
- Gate some WALK_SCENE_EFFECTS contributors behind sceneDissolve
  progress so they ramp in post-reveal.

Acceptance: on /?seed=00 and /?seed=ff first frames, 'theos.sh'
glyphs are legible without squinting; no single seed's palette
erases the title.
close_reason: title face now beats terrain in hit priority and renders with solid block glyph; seed=00/ff first frames legible (verified via puppeteer capture)

title: Spawn camera too high above ground
description:
After theos.sh-cbi (spawn at u=0,v=0.25 with eyeOffset along surface
normal), camera sits noticeably too far from terrain on initial frame —
breaks the ground-level walking POV.

Investigate:
- renderer.eyeOffsetAlongNormal default (0.05) — fine for old spawn
  but visually too tall at the new top-of-tube spawn where the
  ground-relative scale differs.
- whether eye offset should scale with manifold.minorRadius or with
  local surface curvature.
- consider lower default or per-spawn override.

Acceptance: initial frame at /?seed=00 shows player eye at apparent
walking height (terrain dominates near-bottom of frame, not floating
in mid-air).
close_reason: Lowered renderer.eyeOffsetAlongNormal default 0.05→0.02; spawn frame now has near terrain dominating bottom 20 rows (was 14). See commit 2dde5fc.

title: Spawn camera tilt: torus horizon not level
description:
After theos.sh-cbi (spawn at u=0,v=0.25 facing title.center [0,0,0]),
torus appears slightly tilted from initial viewpoint. Horizon line of
torus surface is not horizontal — likely a roll artifact from the
view basis or asymmetric tangent at the spawn pose.

Fix direction: investigate
- whether faceTargetPose's pitch+yaw decomposition implicitly induces
  roll (none expected, but worth checking against ray.ts up vector
  derivation: up = cross(right, fwd) after pitch).
- whether the local tangent basis at (u=0, v=0.25) is rotated
  relative to world horizontal (it is — tU=(0,1,0), n=(0,0,1) for
  default torus; basis is fine, but title billboard plane orientation
  relative to camera up may not align with world XY).
- adjust by adding small roll correction or picking spawn (u, v) where
  tangent basis aligns with world horizon.

Acceptance: torus horizon ring renders horizontally aligned (within ~1
pixel-row of true horizontal) on initial frame at /?seed=00.

title: Restore wave pattern + per-seed multicolor on the root surface scene
description:
Root / surface scene currently looks visually flat / monochromatic and the
seed appears fixed regardless of ?seed=. Two regressions:

1. Wave pattern: the background-wave / curvature animation that previously
   animated across the surface is no longer visible (or no longer wired
   into the walk scene). backgroundWaveEffect is still in
   WALK_SCENE_EFFECTS (src/effects/registry.ts) but its on-screen effect
   is missing.

2. Per-seed multicolor: generateColorScheme(seed) is called in
   src/surface-app.tsx but the rendered output looks identical across
   seeds (try /?seed=00 vs /?seed=ff). Either the scheme isn't being
   applied to the right cells, or the seed itself is being defaulted
   somewhere upstream of the scheme generator.

Investigate:
  - Whether ?seed=<hex> actually flows into the surface backend (e.g.
    a fixed seed used in createGame or makeSurface call).
  - Whether the background-wave effect is producing nonzero contributions
    after the title-billboard refactor (may have been disconnected from
    the surface-cells contributor).
  - Whether scheme.accent/highlight are being routed to the renderer's
    glyph color path or only to background.

Acceptance:
  - /?seed=aa and /?seed=ff produce visibly different color palettes on
    first frame.
  - Background wave animation is visible during walk.
close_reason: Fixed: sha256-derived sub-seed in generateColorScheme + sky branch dropped from surface-cells. Verified /?seed=aa /?seed=ff /?seed=00 give distinct palettes; bg-wave visible on sky.

title: Initial camera should face the title billboard, not the torus surface
description:
On boot of the surface pipeline at /, the camera spawn pose looks at the
torus surface instead of at the diegetic title billboard introduced in
64b9eb2. The first frame should frame the "theos.sh" title so the user
sees it before they start walking.

Current behavior: pose initialized in createPlayer (src/surface-game/player.ts)
with yaw=0, pitch=-0.3 — points along +tU tangent, slightly downward at the
surface. Title is rendered at the torus center via a 'title' HitKind in the
raycast pipeline (src/renderer/ascii-raycast/title.ts) and is offscreen.

Fix direction: pick an initial (u, v, yaw, pitch) at game-create time
(src/surface-game/loop.ts createGame) such that the title billboard's
projected center lies near the screen center on frame 0. Either:
  - hardcode a pose chosen empirically from the title's world placement, OR
  - derive it: aim from the spawn point at the billboard's world position,
    solve for yaw + pitch in the local tangent basis.

Acceptance: navigating to /?seed=00 shows the "theos.sh" title centered
(or near-centered) in the initial frame, before any input.

Verify via tests/visual/surface-walk-effects.test.ts pattern + manual
load.

title: Rework diegetic title to match legacy visual parity
description:
## Why

szv shipped a diegetic billboard (per-char spherical quad) but lost all visual richness of the legacy pre-diegetic title: big ASCII-art letters, shadow halo, seed-shuffled reveal, secondary-color density glyphs via charset-variant. User flagged: "current implementation lacks all features of the original."

Goal: rebuild title rendering to legacy parity while keeping the billboard diegetic (world-space, raycast-intersected, survives walk-away/return, works across seeds).

## Current state (post-szv, HEAD=8e835be)

- `HitKind = 'terrain' | 'artifact' | 'title' | 'sky'` in src/surface-game/types.ts
- src/renderer/ascii-raycast/title.ts: spherical billboard, per-char advance, per-char time-based reveal. Insufficient — looks like plain text on a floating sign.
- src/renderer/ascii-raycast/render.ts: accepts `title?, elapsedMs?`; picks nearest hit; emits `hitKind:'title'` with glyph from intersectTitle.
- src/surface-game/loop.ts: owns `title: TitleMarker`, accumulates `elapsedMs`, threads to renderFrame.
- src/effects/base/surface-cells.ts: title → face layer, accent×1.4, sat = sa*satAt. Uses charOverride.
- Tests: title.test.ts (6), render.test.ts (+2 title cases), surface-cells.test.ts (+2 title cases).
- Visual snapshot tests/visual/surface-walk-effects.test.ts pinned `f28c1c983ccb0476`.

## Legacy references (pre-diegetic, last seen at commit 84625b5)

Read these via `git show 84625b5:<path>`:

- `src/effects/base/text-mask.ts` — drawMaskCanvas, MASK_SCALE=4, stacked vs single layout, fontWeight from `gateParam(seed,'fontVariation','weight')`. Produces face cells + textDensity (3×3 neighbor count).
- `src/effects/base/text-cells.ts` — emits cells: secondary color, FADE_BAND=5, layer=3 (face) v=density/4, layer=1 (shadow) v=0.35 + density/4*0.25. No charOverride (charset-variant picks glyph).
- `src/effects/base/shadow-3d.ts` — projects layerMask=1 (face) along angle = `gateParam(seed,'shadow3D','angle')*2π` to produce shadow mask.
- `src/effects/base/reveal.ts` — REVEAL_TOTAL_MS=6000, shuffle by `(hCol ^ hRow) >>> 0` sort (hashes via sha256First32(concatBytes(seed, SEPARATOR, encode("reveal:col:"+N)))), count = round(total * (elapsed/6000)^1.5).
- `src/effects/base/charset-variant.ts` — 6 palettes, selected by `gate(seed,'charsetVariant')`; renderer: `palette[clampDensityIndex(cell.density)]`.
- `src/effects/base/manifold-genus.ts` — carves layerMask=-1 voids (optional; may skip for diegetic).
- `src/effects/base/text-distortion.ts` — sinusoidal col shift (optional; mask-space port or skip).

## Plan

### 1. Rewrite src/renderer/ascii-raycast/title.ts

```ts
interface TitleMarker {
  center: Vec3;
  text: string;               // 'theos.sh'
  widthWorld: number;
  heightWorld: number;
  // rasterized grids (MASK_SCALE=4, e.g. 256×32 -> 64×8 cells)
  maskW: number;
  maskH: number;
  alpha: Uint8Array;          // 0/255 per sub-pixel
  density: Uint8Array;        // 0..9 per face cell
  shadowMask: Uint8Array;     // 0/1 per cell
  revealOrder: Uint32Array;   // face indices in reveal order
  revealTotalMs: number;      // 6000
}

interface TitleHit {
  distance: number;
  kind: 'face' | 'shadow';
  density: number;
  maskIdx: number;
}

createTitleMarker(t: TunablesShape, seed: Uint8Array): TitleMarker
  // 1. Canvas rasterize text with gateParam(seed,'fontVariation','weight')
  // 2. Build density via 3×3 neighbor count over alpha
  // 3. Build shadowMask via projection along gateParam(seed,'shadow3D','angle')
  // 4. Build revealOrder: sort face cell indices by (hashCol(seed,col) ^ hashRow(seed,row)) >>> 0

intersectTitle(ray, marker, playerPos, elapsedMs): TitleHit | null
  // ray-plane intersect billboard; compute (localU,localV); sample mask
  // gate by reveal count = round(face.length * (elapsedMs/revealTotalMs)^1.5)
  // face hits only if maskIdx within revealed prefix; shadow hits always (or gate separately?)
```

### 2. Add `'title-shadow'` to HitKind

src/surface-game/types.ts — extend union. ShadedCell for title-shadow carries density via luminance.

### 3. Update render.ts

Emit `hitKind: 'title'` (face) or `'title-shadow'` with luminance=density/9, glyph=' ' (charset-variant picks). Keep nearest-hit arbitration.

### 4. Rework src/effects/base/surface-cells.ts title handler

- Use `scheme.secondary` (not accent).
- Face: `cell.value = density / 4; cell.saturation = sa * satAt; cell.layer = 'face';` NO charOverride — let charset-variant palette pick from density.
- Shadow: `cell.value = 0.35 + density * 0.25; cell.layer = 'shadow';` NO charOverride.
- Register charset-variant (or equivalent density-indexed palette) in WALK_SCENE_EFFECTS so title glyphs look right.

### 5. loop.ts / createGame

Pass `seed` into createTitleMarker. Keep elapsedMs accumulation.

### 6. Tests

- title.test.ts: rasterization sanity (alpha non-empty, density bounded), shuffled-reveal determinism (same seed → same order), reveal-count easing, hit kinds (face/shadow), billboard geometry unchanged.
- render.test.ts: title-face AND title-shadow cells visible at pitch=1.3, late-time; reveal gate keeps early face count < late face count.
- surface-cells.test.ts: face uses secondary-tinted HSV + density/4; shadow layer uses 0.35+density*0.25; no charOverride.
- Visual: re-run tests/visual/surface-walk-effects.test.ts, update snapshot hash once rework lands.

## Acceptance

- Title visible across ≥3 seeds with legacy-feeling richness (big letters, halo, seed-variant glyphs).
- Saturation field still modulates title (carry forward from szv).
- Shuffled reveal completes within 6000ms, deterministic per seed.
- Shadow halo renders with secondary color at lower value than face.
- Survives walk-away + return (billboard persists in world).
- surface-smoke + surface-walk-effects green (update hashes if intentional).
- typecheck green (no new errors vs main baseline).

## Risks

- charset-variant effect may not exist in current WALK_SCENE_EFFECTS — may need to port from 84625b5 or add density-indexed glyph selection inline in surface-cells.
- shadow-3d angle projection was screen-space in legacy — needs reformulation in mask-space or billboard-local space.
- manifold-genus + text-distortion touched full-screen layerMask — scope question: port to mask-space, or drop for diegetic.

title: Visual tests non-deterministic due to wall-clock animation
description:
tests/visual/surface-title.test.ts (Task 13) and surface-walk-effects.test.ts (Task 14) pin PNG screenshot hashes. These fail on rerun because the surface renderer animates against performance.now() — two runs at nominally "t=3s" sample different rAF phases.

Options:
1. Deterministic-clock mode: ?t=0.2,3,7 query param that makes app read time from URL not performance.now()
2. Perceptual-diff: pixelmatch with threshold, not exact hash
3. Weaker assertion: canvas non-empty / mean-luminance-in-range instead of exact hash

Related: tests/visual/surface-smoke.test.ts still queries document.querySelector('pre') but canvas replaced <pre> in Task 4. Also broken.

Also: /home/lunaris/.local/bin/chrome-sandboxed had lost +x bit on this machine (EACCES); chmod +x fixed out-of-band. Check CI-parity.

title: Golden frames hashes drifted from baseline
description:
tests/integration/golden-frames.test.ts is failing with 4 hash mismatches against the recorded baseline. Stashing all working-tree changes and re-running confirms the failure is pre-existing on commit 29bcfd3 (core) — independent of theos.sh-dp5.

Either the golden baseline needs to be regenerated (if the drift is a sanctioned renderer change) or the rendering regression needs to be hunted down. First step: bisect between the baseline and 29bcfd3 to find the offending commit.

Output excerpt (one of four):
  hash: 19ff055f → 01a215a5
  hash: fc7b463e → 6684c6e8
  hash: 6e4fed6b → 40e56944
  ...
close_reason: Drift bisected to 1cad388 (world-space wave + edge-fade, sanctioned renderer change). Baselines regenerated via UPDATE_GOLDENS=1; all 4 seeds now pass.

title: Surface pipeline: cannot interact with artifact after reaching it
description:
Pinned to: commit 29bcfd3 (core branch, 2026-04-18) — the commit that
made the surface pipeline the default at /.

Repro:
1. Load / (defaults to surface pipeline).
2. Walk until the placed artifact is reached.
3. Expected: proximity indicator + keypress (Enter) opens the artifact
   detail / content view, as the legacy pipeline does via
   [data-testid="proximity-hint"] and [data-testid="detail-view"].
4. Actual: no proximity feedback, no Enter/interact binding. Player
   can walk onto/through the artifact with no affordance for engaging
   with its content.

Walking + placement + discovery feel great; the dead-end at contact
is the one missing piece keeping surface from parity with legacy.

Scope:
- src/surface-game/artifacts.ts — no proximity threshold / hint state.
- src/surface-game/loop.ts — no Enter/Esc binding, no detail view
  lifecycle.
- src/surface-app.tsx — no detail-view mount parallel to legacy
  src/app.tsx / src/game/detail-view.tsx.

Related: theos.sh-lgx Phase 2 parity criterion "artifact content".
Blocks theos.sh-8vs (Phase 3 legacy removal) — cannot delete legacy
detail view until surface has equivalent.

Acceptance:
- Within N units of the artifact, a hint element appears
  (data-testid="proximity-hint" to match legacy tests).
- Enter while hinted opens content (data-testid="detail-view") with
  the artifact's associated content entry.
- Esc closes back to walking state.

title: Phase 3: remove legacy manifold pipeline
description:
Follow-up to theos.sh-lgx. The surface pipeline is now the default at /;
?pipeline=legacy still opts into the old manifold pipeline for parity
testing.

Once parity is confirmed, delete:
- src/manifold/
- src/applicator/
- src/viewport/
- src/game/
- src/app.tsx
- src/renderer/ (legacy bits only — confirm no shared code with surface)
- src/renderers/ (confirm)
- src/pipeline-flag.ts + test (no longer needed)

And simplify src/index.tsx to boot SurfaceApp unconditionally.

Update/remove legacy-pinned visual tests:
- tests/visual/landing-smoke.test.ts (?pipeline=legacy)
- tests/visual/game-flow.test.ts (?pipeline=legacy, uses proximity-hint/detail-view testids)

Do not start until surface pipeline has reached parity for: title page,
walking, artifact content reveal (Enter/Esc detail view).
notes: Unblocked 2026-04-18: epic theos.sh-6uu complete. Surface pipeline now has parity for title page (TITLE_SCENE_EFFECTS + reveal dissolve), walking (WALK_SCENE_EFFECTS + surface-cells bridge), and artifact detail view (scheme-aware). Ready to start when parity verified in-browser.

title: Fix PRNG determinism break in P3 feature-biased artifact placement
close_reason: Fixed in 03e7ec9: u/v drawn from PRNG unconditionally, feature point overwrites when present. Stream advancement constant across backend-on/backend-off paths. Regression test added comparing radius/offset/spikes across both paths for same seed. 302/302 tests green.

title: Upgrade geodesic integrator from RK2 midpoint to RK4 per spec
close_reason: Fixed in 8d6fb3a: geodesicStep replaced with canonical RK4 on coupled (u,v,uDot,vDot) ODE — 4 accel evals per substep, O(h^4) local truncation. Metric-norm tolerance tightened 0.02→0.005. New RK4 test at larger ds/fewer substeps. 303/303 tests green.

title: Fix phantom hit in marchTerrain coarse→fine transition
close_reason: Fixed in d890312: prevD recomputed after each coarse stride as true signed distance at new position (mirroring init block). Before: 0.01924 world-unit hit error at coarse→fine transition (≈ one fineStep). After: 0.000000 (exact analytic crossing). Regression test uses amplitude=1e-4 flat surface so analytic base-torus hit is known. 304/304 green.

title: Integrate the /surface/ pipeline into the main / game entry
description:
v0 ships the new surface-first manifold pipeline at /surface/ as a standalone Vite
entry. The existing / game still runs the old ambient [x,y,z] manifold
(src/manifold/*, src/applicator/*, src/viewport/*).

verify the new pipeline matches or exceeds the old game's behavior for the

title: Diagnose Chrome VMEM growth when serving theos.sh (likely caching issue)
description:
When serving theos.sh via the dev server, Chrome's virtual memory usage grows over time. User suspects a caching issue — probably something on the page is retaining references (texture atlases, character cells, mesh buffers, or ASCII frame history).

Repro:
- Start dev server (bun dev or equivalent)
- Load the site in Chrome
- Leave tab open, interact with the engine (walk around)
- Observe VMEM grow without bounding

Investigation steps:
1. Reproduce locally and capture chrome://memory-internals + a Performance > Memory heap snapshot timeline.
2. Identify the allocator: is it the text-cells effect retaining past frames? Is it Three.js geometry/material not disposed? Is it a Solid.js signal chain holding prior mesh references?
3. Check the render loop for per-frame allocations that never get released (array.slice, new Float32Array, etc).
4. Check WebGL resources (buffers, textures) for missing .dispose() on unmount / reseed.
5. Check the service worker / HTTP cache — if assets are loaded per-reseed, browsers may accumulate entries.
6. Fix the leak; confirm VMEM is flat across a 10-minute walk session.

Acceptance:
- VMEM is bounded (no monotone growth) across 10 min of continuous interaction.
- No WebGL context-lost warnings from resource exhaustion.

Reported by user; likely pre-dates current brainstorming work.

title: game-flow visual test times out at /?pipeline=legacy navigation

title: Signal-bus subscriptions leak on scene transition
description:
SurfaceApp.onMount registers all TITLE_SCENE_EFFECTS. On dissolve→walk, only the cell contributors named in TITLE_EFFECTS_TO_UNREGISTER are removed via Applicator.unregister. The underlying signal-bus subscriptions (buildMask, maskReady, frameBegin, buildFields) from reveal, text-mask, manifold-genus, text-cells stay alive for the entire walk scene.

Benign today: reveal's frameBegin handler runs every frame on stale revealedMask but no cell contributor reads it in walk. Latent: any future effect that reacts to these handlers' side effects could break.

Fix: Applicator.unregister needs to forward removal to the signal bus too, OR SurfaceApp should capture EffectHandles from e.register(app) and dispose them at transition.
close_reason: Superseded by 64b9eb2 (reinstate title as diegetic billboard). No scene transitions remain — only WALK_SCENE_EFFECTS register at boot, no per-transition unregister path. Original leak vector eliminated by deleting the title scene.

title: Hardcoded TITLE_EFFECTS_TO_UNREGISTER list drifts from registry
description:
src/surface-app.tsx hardcodes TITLE_EFFECTS_TO_UNREGISTER = ['text-mask', 'text-cells', 'reveal', 'manifold-genus']. Should be derived: TITLE_SCENE_EFFECTS.map(e => e.name).filter(n => !WALK_SCENE_EFFECTS.map(e => e.name).includes(n)).

Adding a new title-only effect to the registry means remembering to update this const. Derived form would self-sync.
close_reason: Superseded by 64b9eb2 (reinstate title as diegetic billboard). Title-only scene machine removed; walk is the only scene. No TITLE_EFFECTS_TO_UNREGISTER list exists in src/surface-app.tsx anymore.

title: A/D keys strafe opposite of expected direction
description:
In the surface-pipeline walking loop, A and D strafe the player in
the opposite direction relative to conventional FPS mapping (A = left,
D = right).

Location: src/surface-game/player.ts:83-86

  const right: Vec3 = [-sinY*tU[0] + cosY*tR[0], ...];
  const rStep = (keys.d ? 1 : 0) + (keys.a ? -1 : 0);

Either the `right` basis vector is pointing to the player's left (sign
error in the yaw rotation at line 83) or the rStep polarity is flipped
(D should contribute negative along this basis).

Likely fix: swap the rStep polarity OR flip the sign convention in
the `right` vector derivation — whichever is symmetric with the Q/E
fix on theos.sh-hot.

Related: theos.sh-hot (Q/E yaw inverted). Same root suspicion — the
view-basis handedness (tU forward vs. tR = n × tU) may be using a
left-handed convention while the input mapping assumes right-handed.
Fix both together.

Acceptance: with default yaw, pressing D moves the player to the
right side of the current view; A moves left.

title: Q/E keys rotate screen opposite of expected direction
description:
In the surface-pipeline walking loop, Q and E keys control player yaw
but the on-screen world rotation goes the wrong way relative to user
expectation.

Location: src/surface-game/player.ts:58-59

  if (keys.q) pose.yaw = wrapYaw(pose.yaw - t.walk.yawRate * dt);
  if (keys.e) pose.yaw = wrapYaw(pose.yaw + t.walk.yawRate * dt);

Likely fix: swap the signs (Q = +yawRate, E = -yawRate) or invert the
yaw→view-direction mapping in the renderer — whichever matches the
FPS convention (Q looks left, E looks right, world rotates the
opposite direction under the fixed camera).

Verify against: tests/visual/surface-smoke.test.ts and manual play via
?pipeline=surface on /.

Acceptance: pressing Q rotates the visible terrain to the right of
screen (user "looks left"); pressing E rotates it to the left.

title: Rust+WASM port of ASCII raycaster hot path (Path B)
description:
After Path A perf pass (adaptive sphere-trace, scalar inline, grid sampler) the pure-TS ASCII marcher hits ~43fps @ 160x60. WASM port could push this to 120+fps and enable larger viewports / higher fine-step resolution.

Current TS hot path (`src/renderer/ascii-raycast/march.ts`):
- ~10k rays/frame
- Per-ray adaptive sphere-trace + fine-phase parametric SDF
- Bottleneck is Math.sqrt + Math.atan2 counts, not JS overhead

Port candidates:
1. `marchTerrain` + `baseTorusSDF` + `sampleGridPeriodic` — pure math, no JS deps, ideal WASM candidates
2. `makeRays` ray construction — matrix-heavy, less hot
3. Whole `renderFrame` — includes artifact intersect + glyph selection, more surface area

Approach:
- Rust crate with `wasm-bindgen`, compiled via `wasm-pack build --target web`
- Pass height grid as `&[f32]` slice, ray origins/dirs as `&[f32; 6]`
- Return glyph index array
- JS side translates glyph index → character via existing ramp

Benchmark target: ≥3x over current TS path (120+ fps @ 160x60) to justify the build complexity.

Blocker: none. Path A is green and shipped.
Distinct from theos.sh-5wk (which is Tier 2+ Three.js vs custom WASM eval).

title: /surface/ route reportedly shows landing wave+title in browser
description:
User reports visiting /surface/ sees background-wave + title from landing page at /, not the raycast ASCII frame. Curl of http://localhost:3000/surface/ (vite dev) returns correct isolated surface/index.html — no wave, no title, only #root + surface-entry.tsx. Surface-entry imports no landing code (verified). No service worker, no vite history fallback.

Theories:
- Browser cache of / served stale on /surface/ visit
- User visited /surface (no trailing slash) redirected/mismatched
- Prev dev server stale; browser served cached bundle

Repro needed: user hard-refresh /surface/?seed=2a with devtools Network "Disable cache". If still shows wave, inspect DOM for source.
close_reason: Fixed in 4486ac5: /surface (no slash) was falling through Vite SPA index.html fallback to the landing page content. Added 301 redirect for bare sub-route paths in both dev (vite plugin) and prod (bun server). 277/277 tests green.

title: R2 coarse-rejection wiring for ascii-raycast marcher
description:
Task 14 review surfaced an architecture lie: renderFrame was computing a height grid (materializeHeightGrid) every frame and passing it into marchTerrain, but the marcher never consulted it — just fell through to analytic signed-distance. Cleanup commit dropped the grid materialization from the render path to stop the dead work.

Follow-up: actually wire R2 (spec-ref) coarse AABB/height rejection into the marcher so rays that obviously miss the tube can skip the per-step analytic signed distance. Grid can be lazily rebuilt on rebuild() when amplitude/heightGridN mutate.

Scope: coarse-rejection only. Do not touch analytic refinement step.
close_reason: Fixed in 3caae13: ray vs bounding-sphere early-out + entry-advance wired before adaptive sphere-trace loop. 280/280 green. Frame time 23.09ms → 11.22ms (2x speedup over prior pass, 98x cumulative from pre-opt baseline).

title: Upgrade artifact placement from P1 (random uniform) to P3 (terrain-feature biased)
description:
P1 ships first: seed deterministically picks N artifact positions (u_i, v_i) uniformly in the unit square, with N a small constant (3–7). Each artifact sits at embed(u_i, v_i) + d · n̂(u_i, v_i). Minimum 1 guaranteed per seed.

P3 upgrade: artifacts are placed at geometrically meaningful points on the surface:
- Local maxima of h(u,v) (hilltops)
- Local minima of h(u,v) (valley floors)
- Saddle points / points of high |Gaussian curvature|
- Near handles / high-genus features (once A3 multi-patch topology lands)

Why upgrade: P1 placements feel scattered. P3 makes artifacts feel *sited* — crowning hilltops, marking saddles near a hole, etc. The world reads as designed rather than sprinkled. Strong aesthetic payoff.

How: sample-grid the derived scalar field (|K|, ∇h, or a hand-tuned "interestingness" combinator), run a maxima-finder with minimum-separation filter, take the top-N points.

Depends on:
- P1 (baseline placement working)
- Access to derivative samples of the height field (already exposed by I3 core: normalAt, metricAt)
- Optionally: A3 multi-patch atlas (theos.sh-57n) if we want to bias toward handle sites.
close_reason: Fixed in 72867aa: findExtremaCandidates grid-scans h(u,v) for periodic local max/min; pickWithMinSeparation applies toroidal Chebyshev min-sep; placeArtifacts uses these when a backend is provided. 294/294 green.

title: Upgrade spiky-ball artifact from S1 (primitive ray test) to S2 (SDF raymarch)
description:
S1 ships first: spiky ball = sphere + cone-spike primitives (or radial-modulated sphere), placed at embed(u_a, v_a) + offset·n̂. R1's per-cell ray test intersects (height grid, artifact primitives), nearest hit wins. Closed-form sphere-ray intersection; occlusion by terrain is free.

S2 upgrade: artifact becomes a signed-distance function (e.g. max(sphere, -∪(spike cones)), or a star-polytope SDF). The whole engine switches to SDF-first rendering: terrain height grid also gets SDF-ified (or dual-tracked), raymarcher marches a unified distance field.

Why upgrade: SDFs compose cleanly — you can smooth-union artifacts together, deform them, animate them, and the whole thing is a single march. Higher tiers (esp. WASM raymarcher in theos.sh-5wk) naturally want SDFs anyway.

When: once the WASM/SDF renderer tier in theos.sh-5wk is being prototyped. Don't do it inside the ASCII tier alone — that would force R1 to become a full raymarcher without benefit.

Depends on: theos.sh-5wk (WASM raymarcher eval) landing, and an SDF representation for the terrain height field existing.

title: Upgrade periodic noise from N2 (4D projection) to N1 (tunable Fourier spectrum)
description:
N2 ships first: h(u,v) sampled from 4D simplex noise at (cos 2πu, sin 2πu, cos 2πv, sin 2πv). Exact periodicity, natural-landscape look, seed → noise permutation table.

N1 upgrade: h(u,v) = Σ_{k,l} a_kl · sin(2π(k·u + φ_kl)) · sin(2π(l·v + ψ_kl)), with seed-driven coefficients.

Why upgrade: N1 gives *direct control of the spectrum*. You can:
- Set a sharp high-frequency cutoff to enforce a curvature budget analytically (|K| bounded by bounded second derivatives).
- Tune the power-law (e.g. 1/(k²+l²)^α) to pick between "smooth hills" and "fractal-rough" terrain from a single seed knob.
- Expose a handful of dominant modes to the player/viewer as interpretable parameters.

N2 cannot do any of this cleanly — the noise spectrum is baked in.

When: once the engine is stable on N2 and we want a "tunable" or "stylized" terrain mode. Not urgent.

Depends on: N2 shipping and the curvature budget being characterized empirically.

title: Evaluate WASM custom raymarcher vs Three.js for higher rendering tiers
description:
The original architecture-tiers memory assumed Three.js for Tier 3 and deeper. On reflection, Three.js may not be the most efficient backend for this engine:

- Non-Euclidean geometry: Three.js's rasterization pipeline assumes a flat ambient space. Geodesic integration on a curved manifold doesn't compose cleanly with its default rendering model.
- Raymarching-heavy workload: deeper tiers will raymarch SDFs, integrate geodesics per-pixel via RK4, and sample custom metric tensors. This is shader-heavy math, not triangle-heavy scenes — Three.js's abstractions add overhead without helping.
- Control: a custom WASM (Rust → wasm32) raymarcher gives us direct access to the metric g_ij, Christoffel symbols, and atlas transition functions without marshalling through JS/WebGL object graphs.

Investigate:
1. Prototype a minimal Rust+WASM raymarcher against the I3 backend (calls into JS backend or reimplements pure-fn sampling in Rust).
2. Benchmark against a Three.js baseline rendering the same scene.
3. Compare code complexity, perf, and how naturally each expresses non-Euclidean walking / geodesic rays.
4. Decide: Three.js / custom WASM / hybrid for Tier 2 and deeper.

Does NOT affect Tier 3 (ASCII) which uses R1 height-grid raycasting in pure TS.

Depends on: R1 ASCII tier shipping first so there's a working reference implementation to benchmark against.

title: Upgrade ASCII renderer from R1 (height-grid raycast) to R2 (mesh rasterize)
description:
R1 ships first: one-time materializeHeightGrid(backend, N), per-frame per-cell raycast against the periodic grid with torus wrap, shade by surface-normal · view-direction. Tiny march loop, ASCII-native, wrap comes free from grid periodicity.

R2 upgrade: call materializeMesh(backend, N), project vertices through a camera matrix, rasterize into a float z-buffer + normal-buffer at terminal resolution, map luminance → ASCII ramp.

Why upgrade: if/when a higher tier exists that wants a shared triangle mesh (e.g. a WebGL or WASM renderer), R2 lets the ASCII tier consume the same materializer. One mesh shared across tiers beats two independent materializations.

Why not now: R1 is smaller, simpler, and the height-field→raycast path handles the torus topology naturally. R2 is valuable only once another tier actually needs the mesh.

Depends on: R1 shipping; higher-tier renderer choice (see related bead on WASM raymarcher vs Three.js).

title: Derive walking physics from induced metric (C3 completion)
description:
Demo ships C1: seed-driven periodic height field h(u,v) on the unit square, rendered as a bumpy torus. Initial walking can be naive — e.g., move (u,v) at fixed speed ignoring local stretch — which is visually OK for gentle bumps but drifts from true geodesic motion as curvature grows.

Upgrade to C3: walking is genuine motion along induced metric g_ij = (∂φ/∂uⁱ · ∂φ/∂uⁱ) pulled back from the embedding φ(u,v) = (u, v, h(u,v)). Forward-key motion integrates the geodesic equation in (u,v) rather than moving at constant (u,v) speed. Makes "walk forward up a hill" feel right (you slow down going up) and locks walking to the same surface the camera is rendering.

Depends on:
- C1 height field + rendering being solid
- A concrete "player state" (position on chart + tangent direction) that the walker can evolve
close_reason: Fixed in bfe6544: stepPlayer seeds a metric-normalized velocity and integrates the geodesic ODE via RK2 midpoint substeps. Flat-metric sanity tests, curved-torus metric-norm preservation, and a chord-length invariant all hold. 301/301 tests green.

title: Expand atlas from single-torus (A1) to multi-patch forced-handle (A3)
description:
Demo manifold starts as A1 — single unit square with opposite edges identified (torus). Good: finite, closed, exercises the atlas/transition-function code path. Limitation: topology is always a torus; the seed has nothing to say about genus.

Upgrade path: A3 — larger atlas (16+ square patches) with seed-biased gluing that guarantees at least one non-trivial handle. Lets the seed actually express topology, makes "walk around a hole to the other side" reliable on any seed rather than a torus-only phenomenon.

Depends on:
- A1 torus demo being solid (atlas types, edge gluing, walking handoff all proven)
- Bead theos.sh-x6p (polygonal upgrade) still pending decision — A3 could land before or after B

Not blocking the initial demo.

title: Upgrade manifold atlas from squares to polygonal tiles
description:
Current demo manifold (option A in the brainstorm) uses unit-square chart patches with edge-gluing. This is simple and gives real topology (torus, genus-g via edge identifications), but constrains the set of manifolds we can express cleanly.

Upgrade path: polygonal tiles (option B) — triangles/hexagons/4g-gons with per-edge gluing. Unlocks standard genus-g presentations (4g-gon with canonical edge identifications) and more natural curvature distribution.

Depends on:
- Demo atlas implementation (option A) being solid first
- Renderer not baking in 4-edges-per-patch assumption

Not blocking the initial demo.

title: 3D world rendering brainstorm
description:
The rendered world currently reads as 2D rather than 3D. The engine has
the pieces for volumetric cues (layerMask with face/shadow, text-cells,
curvature-field, shadow-3d modulator, SDF genus modulators) but the
composite still collapses to a flat layer stack.

This is a **brainstorm / design** task, not an implementation:
- Identify which cues are actually contributing vs. canceling each other
  out in the current pipeline (priority ordering, layer overrides,
  saturation/value choices).
- Consider parallax, depth from viewport motion, character-scale cues,
  perspective curvature, explicit z-ordering of glyphs, SDF normals for
  shading — and pick a small set to prototype.
- Consider whether the manifold curvature field should modulate glyph
  choice/density/color to imply depth rather than just warp.
- Output: a spec in docs/superpowers/specs/ describing the chosen
  approach(es) before any code lands.

Deferred from the 2026-04-16 session where small fixes (screen-edge
shadow fade + ASCII [enter] tooltip) were handled inline; the 3D
question was explicitly scoped out as needing its own brainstorm.

title: Pretext is a layout engine, not an animation engine
description: github.com/chenglou/pretext (@chenglou/pretext) is a canvas text measurement/layout library (line-breaking, bidi, emoji sizing), NOT a text animation library as assumed during brainstorming. It has no dist/ dir (ships source only) and exports prepare(text, font) + layout(prepared, maxWidth) for accurate text wrapping in canvas contexts. For the thin slice, the detail view uses plain HTML with a JS-driven character reveal. Pretext may be useful later for the Phase 2 in-world canvas text rendering (theos.sh-osq) where accurate layout on the ASCII grid matters.
close_reason: Context captured. Detail view ships with plain HTML char reveal; pretext usage deferred to Phase 2 canvas text (theos.sh-osq) which already exists. No open action item.

title: Evaluate pretext fallback path
description: If 'bun add pretext' (or github:chenglou/pretext) does not yield a clean ESM build compatible with Solid/Vite, implement the text-reveal animation in-house using the existing Applicator + NarrativeOrchestrator (src/narrative/orchestrator.ts) staggered-reveal queue machinery. Only triggered if the A path fails during thin-slice implementation.

title: Path-validity server endpoint
description: Extend the visibility endpoint (contents+positions) with the third threat-model concern: server tracks the path the client walked and validates it meets a criterion before unlocking content. Wires up PathSubmitRequest in src/state/types.ts. Requires actual puzzle/validation content to exist — not applicable until artifacts carry path criteria.

title: Directional gradient hints
description: Extend the visibility endpoint to return not just a single hint cell but a small patch of cells whose curvature/density subtly pull the eye toward the artifact's actual location. Replaces the thin-slice single-cell perturbation. Needs a direction-leaking design that doesn't expose more position information than the hint already does.

title: Detail view: in-world expansion
description: Replace the full-viewport takeover detail view with in-world expansion — the artifact cell itself expands in place to fill the viewport as text glyphs emerge from that cell, no separate UI layer. Preserves the 'preview is the game' ethos end to end. Highest animation/layout complexity; postponed until the thin slice proves out with the simpler takeover view.

title: Seed-randomized key bindings
description: Swap the game's fixed WASD/arrow bindings at / to use the existing InputMapper class (src/input/input-mapper.ts) which derives random key→Op mappings from the seed. Deferred from the thin slice because seed-random controls paired with a sparse map read as broken rather than mysterious. Enable once the world has enough artifacts to make the discovery texture land.

title: Raycast runs during title scene (wasted work)
description:
src/surface-app.tsx loop() calls game.frame() (which runs the full raycast march + artifact intersection) every frame, including during the title intro (6-8 seconds). Title scene doesn't use frameRef during render — surface-cells isn't registered until walk transition.

Gate game.frame() behind sceneState !== 'title', or accept the waste as negligible (~80ms/frame off the budget during title).

title: ShadedCell.depth emitted by raycast but never consumed
description:
src/surface-game/types.ts ShadedCell has a depth: number field. src/renderer/ascii-raycast/render.ts sets it. src/effects/base/surface-cells.ts and src/surface-app.tsx never read it.

Either delete the field (YAGNI) or use it — e.g., depth-based glyph dithering, atmospheric fade in surface-cells, etc. Spec §"reinterpret curv/sat fields from raycast normals/depth" (step 9) mentions depth-reinterpretation as a future extension.

title: marchTerrain signed-distance is not a true SDF far from surface
description:
Current signedDistanceToSurface in src/renderer/ascii-raycast/march.ts projects a ℝ³ point onto the bumpy torus via nearest-(u,v) inversion of the base-torus parametrization, then dots (p - φ(u,v)) with n̂(u,v). This is correct *near* the surface (small amplitude A, points within a few tube-widths) but becomes a poor distance estimate far away: (u,v) returned by atan2-based inversion is the nearest point on the *base* torus, not on the bumpy one, and the projection can jump discontinuously across the torus hole.

Symptom risk: marching rays that start far from the surface (large pitch offsets, distant eyes) may step past the real surface or report false-positive crossings.

Fix: replace with a proper SDF — either (a) analytic torus SDF + bounded amplitude correction, or (b) bisection-style inversion seeded from the ray origin's ring coordinates, or (c) sphere-tracing with a conservative Lipschitz bound. Option (a) is probably cheapest.

Gated on: we have not yet observed this in practice because eye lives on the surface. File for when we give the player fly mode or far-camera debug view.

title: Runtime-derived curvature budget (B3): auto-bound noise from walking step and flatness tolerance
description:
B2 ships: seed samples (amplitude A, freq cap K_max) from a hand-calibrated safe envelope so |K|·ε stays under threshold.

B3 upgrade: given walking step ε and target flatness tolerance τ (e.g. "surface normal changes by ≤ τ degrees per player step"), solve for the tightest (A, K_max) pair that satisfies the invariant and renormalize the noise.

Why upgrade: B2's envelope is hand-tuned once and doesn't adapt to changes in ε (player speed, zoom level, subdivision of walking into sub-steps for geodesic integration). B3 makes the locally-near-flat invariant a derived guarantee rather than an empirical one.

When: late-stage, after the walking physics (C3) is derived from the induced metric and we care about formal invariants. Not before.

Depends on: C3 geodesic walking being live (bead theos.sh-3fk) — the walking step ε is only well-defined once you're integrating along geodesics rather than constant-(u,v) shuffling.

title: Per-pixel (WebGPU) renderer
description: Future high-end renderer from the effect-applicator spec (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-14-effect-applicator-design.md:686). Implements Renderer interface but consumes field handles (curvature, saturation, layer mask) plus seed for shader-side derivations rather than cell-discrete Frame. Requires new World description type and renderer-kind switch in applicator.

title: Breadcrumb trail to artifact
description: Faint visible trail/gradient from origin toward the artifact to gently guide first-time visitors. Deferred from artifact-placement design; phase 2 once there are 3+ artifacts to guide between.
